headline: Dobey ends televised losing run with win over Schmidt
standfirst: Chris Dobey beat Jan Schmidt 5-2 at the Grand Slam of Darts after losing his opening match at four straight TV events.
body: Chris Dobey broke a streak of four consecutive televised opening-round defeats by beating Jan Schmidt 5-2 in his first match at the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton on Saturday.
Dobey averaged 98.66 to Schmidt's 78.73 and hit five of his nine attempts at a double. Schmidt converted only two of 18, and Dobey's best checkout of the match was 96. Both men threw two maximums.

The result matters because Dobey has enjoyed a strong season on the Pro Tour, winning three Players Championship titles, yet had failed to carry that form onto the TV stage. Afterwards he described how quickly belief can drain away once a match starts to go wrong, saying it is "a lonely place" up there when things are not working, according to Dartsnews.

He was also frank about the contest itself, crediting his win partly to the chances his opponent wasted. In the new three-player group format only the group winner progresses, so a first win is valuable.
Dobey's next match is against Martin Schindler on Tuesday. A win there would take him into the last 16 whatever happens between Schindler and Schmidt.
